source.title: Words Before Pixels: Selective Modality Routing for Vision-Language Model Unlearning
source.authors: Laura Yao; H. Zhang; Jinhao Duan; Si-Jia Liu; Tian-Long Chen

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Uses unlearning methods, including NPO and RMU comparators, to study modality routing, but does not test whether post-unlearning recovery attacks restore knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper measures forgetting and retention after VLM unlearning, but reports no recovery attacks by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting. Its unlearning metrics are relevant background findings but do not measure any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study proposes and benchmarks a VLM unlearning data-routing method (ModRoute) using NPO, with RMU and GradDiff as comparators. It reports only forgetting and utility metrics after unlearning. It applies no recovery attack (relearning, activation edits, quantization, rephrasing or jailbreaks), so it cannot bear on whether unlearned knowledge is recoverable. Nor does it claim robustness to such attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that VLM unlearning depends on the representation, composition and per-sample modality routing of forget data, not only on the objective. Text-included mixtures strengthen forgetting, and gradient-guided routing gives the best forgetting–utility trade-off among the policies they evaluate.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies VLM modality representation and gradient-guided routing with NPO-style unlearning; it does not reproduce or test the post-unlearning recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported forgetting–utility outcomes vary with modality composition, switch ratio, routing selection, dataset, and model.

fits_no_version.finding: Text-heavy and text-included forget mixtures give higher forgetting than image-only or multimodal-only sets on VLGuard and COVID memes. This holds even at a matched 341- or 441-example budget (Tables 4–5). Gradient-guided routing beats random routing on the unlearning–utility score across LLaVA, InternVL3 and Qwen3-VL-4B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLM unlearning, the modality representation of forget examples changes the forgetting–utility trade-off, and selective text routing improves it.

fits_no_version.finding: On modality-decomposed VLGuard test sets, unsafe behaviour on text-only inputs appears easier to unlearn than on image-only inputs (Fig. 12, values only in the figure).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting after VLM unlearning generalises unevenly across input modalities.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026, as stated in the paper
record.problems: The study reports no tests of the recovery mechanisms in the claim, so it cannot establish whether unlearned knowledge is recoverable. Some results are presented in figures without exact values; the paper also notes that the findings apply most directly to language-expressible targets.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted most modality-mixing sweep conditions, detailed utility metrics, and additional seed/model results to stay concise; see Figure 2, Tables 3–6, Figures 3–12, and Tables 8–10. The selected rows summarize the reported modality and routing effects.

untested.parts: No simple attacks are applied to check whether the forgotten behaviour returns. The forget metrics are judge-scored refusal/irrelevance rates, three-way harmfulness accuracy and recall, not knowledge accuracy near chance.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No quantization of the unlearned weights.

No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context recovery attack. Appendix H.1 evaluates forgetting on image-only and text-only test variants, but as a modality-generalisation measure, not a recovery attack.
ModRoute is not evaluated against any recovery attack and does not claim attack robustness.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. They are the study's own method compared with baselines and ablations, which is appropriate for a T4 study. The numbers match Tables 1, 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10. This is not an original source. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether simple attacks recover targeted knowledge after unlearning.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether knowledge is blocked rather than deleted.
No recovery tests using rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
ModRoute is not evaluated for resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.
